reason: The cited lines show the tool reads database metadata/details via a connector, including table schemas, row counts, comments, indexes, stored procedure parameters/definitions, and returns those results, so SECRET is supported. They do not show arbitrary host code execution; executeSQL is used for a readonly SELECT COUNT query, not host execution. They do not show sending agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination or any external write/message, so SINK is not supported. Although returned database fields could in some deployments contain user-controlled text, these lines alone do not establish attacker control over the returned content, so UNTRUSTED is insufficient.
